constraints: Queued mid-run input is deliberately classified by the model at the round boundary (the code says the caller cannot know), so a user-picked interrupt, steer or queue split button contradicts a documented design ruling and needs an explicit decision. Buffered frames and queued text hold content, so ZDR turns stay memory-only (compose notes the ZDR path does not buffer). The compose files read configure no model-gateway replicas, so multi-replica safety hardens a topology that is not deployed; Dragonfly runs cache-mode at 256 MB shared and can evict, and Redis becoming a hard dependency needs a down-behaviour rule. Ordering across replicas needs idempotent operation ids.
approachAdjustment: Remove "turn on the Redis stream buffer in every environment" (already set in the compose block; only confirm it is deployed). Reword the problem: graceful redeploys are covered by drain, so the loss window is a crash, OOM or replica move. Scope shared state to cancel and enqueue routed through a request_id-keyed NATS subject, as the in-code notes propose, and reuse session-core idempotency for durable receipts rather than a new store. Drop the editable queue and split send button from this item unless the owner overrides the model-classifies design.

verdictReason: Real but a scale-readiness hardening for a single-replica deployment with drain and Redis resume already shipped, and it is not a precondition for durable runs because approvals already persist in session-core; the queue UX part needs a design decision first.
